transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me a bit about what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been feeling really depressed, sad, and down for a very long time now. This low mood has been going on constantly for about two years and five months. It just feels like a heavy weight that I can't seem to shake off.
During these past two years and five months, have there been any periods of a few weeks or more where your mood improved significantly, or has the sadness been present almost every single day?

No, there haven't been any breaks or times where I felt better. The sadness and depressed mood have been there almost every single day for the entire two years and five months. It has been completely constant without any relief.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were [Major Depressive Disorder, Persistent Depressive Disorder]. The patient reports a continuous depressed mood lasting over two years without any symptom-free intervals, which aligns with the diagnostic criteria for Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia). Major Depressive Disorder typically requires a distinct episode, and the absence of any relief during this 29-month period strongly points toward the chronic nature of Persistent Depressive Disorder.
